name: Clematis

project_scope.note: Approved B006 native Clematis set. C. terniflora remains a non-native comparison outside this install.

shared_traits: woody or perennial climbing vines with opposite leaves
petal-like sepals rather than true petals
achenes often bearing persistent elongated styles/beaks
priority: length and plumosity of achene beaks
study_strategy.warning: Do not identify leatherflowers by color alone; sepal margin architecture and fruit beaks are critical.

quick_key.if: small open white/cream 4-sepal flowers on separate male/female vines + very long plumose seed tails
nodding blue/reddish-purple leathery urn + expanded/crispate recurved sepal tips + short weakly hairy achene beaks
nodding true rose-red/scarlet leathery urn + non-expanded non-crispate sepal margins + longer plumose achene beaks

shared_genus_characters.look_here_first: Confirm a climbing vine with opposite leaves, then inspect the flower: the showy parts are sepals, not petals. Use mature sepal shape and the later achene head for species-level work.
shared_genus_characters.shared: Project Clematis are climbing perennials with opposite leaves, petaloid sepals, numerous stamens and pistils, and aggregate achenes with persistent styles.

species_comparison_matrix.primary: Small open pale flower rather than a leathery urn
species_comparison_matrix.secondary: Very long plumose persistent styles on mature achenes
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Do not identify from vine habit alone.

species_comparison_matrix.primary: Nodding leathery urn with expanded, crispate, recurved sepal tips
species_comparison_matrix.secondary: Shorter, weakly hairy achene beaks in the current project comparison

species_comparison_matrix.primary: Nodding leathery urn with non-expanded, non-crispate sepal margins
species_comparison_matrix.secondary: Longer, more plumose achene beaks than the project C. pitcheri comparison
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Red color is memorable but not diagnostic by itself.

overlap_and_cautions: Flower color is secondary; inspect sepal margins and tips.
Opposite divided leaves establish the genus but do not reliably separate these species.
Use mature fruit for achene-beak comparisons.
If a mature sepal edge is not visible, keep a leatherflower ID provisional.

realistic_lookalikes.separate_by: Require Clematis reproductive architecture: petaloid sepals, many free stamens and pistils, then aggregate achenes with persistent styles.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.purpose: Show open flower versus urn and expose the sepal tips.
Show expanded/crispate/recurved versus non-expanded sepal margins.
Compare persistent style/beak length and plumosity.

diagnostic_review_handoffs: If mature sepal-tip structure cannot be verified, request a targeted flower-side macro rather than forcing the species ID.
Any species outside the current three-species project set goes to Taxonomy + Diagnostic Review before scope changes.
